title: Palms and succulents at Jacuzzi
description: The palm at the foot of the stairs is from Taiwan, an Arenga engleri, which is a multi-trunking shrubby species that is relatively slow growing in cool summer/mild winter SF Bay Area locations, and therefore is not likely to outgrow this spot any time soon.  Next to it, and behind the trunk of the Coast Live Oak, is a favorite large growing, nearly everblooming Salvia splendens 'Vanhouttii', with deep red flowers.  The taller palm beyond the jacuzzi is a stripped Trachycarpus fortunei, showing how colorful and interesting the trunk can be when the hairy sheaths of the older leaves are removed to reveal the trunk.

title: Courtyard view back to entry
description: This shows how the front courtyard steps down in grade, and is about 3 to 4.5 feet lower than the sidewalk outside the wall.  Again, raised planter walls were used at the inside to mask the apparent height of the walls, and draped with the Stauntonia hexaphylla vine from the front, along with a variegated shrubby Clerodendrum trichotomum 'Harlequin' and Mathiasella bupleuroides in the lower raised planter.

title: Detail of Entry Gate
description: The gate is hinged so that it can open fully or just the gate opens with the side panel fixed.  Glass block was inset within the metal gate frame, and sandblasted with a decorative etched and stylized palm leaf.

title: Looking back towards the jacuzzi from lower patio
Tropical setting with palms and succulents near the jacuzzi
View looking down from terrace
description: The narrow left over garden space between the curved stairs and house wall is a very protected location.  The slow growing Howeia forsteriana, or Kentia Palm, was used below the cantilevered deck above to soften the blank walls, and give a lush jungly look to this part of the garden.  Also planted here are Heliconia schiedeana and Impatiens oliveiri.

title: Fire and Ice
description: The San Francisco East Bay has such a mild winter climate, that it is easily possible to have this sort of color explosion any season you want, even winter.  These plants were installed already blooming in December, and are still happily blooming away in May.  Another reason to put up with the high cost of living here, it never gets old...

title: Looking down from mid level terrace
description: A flowering Hardenbergia violaceae 'Canoelands' is planted to cover the fence, and this has the benefit of blooming nearly twice as long as the more common 'Happy Wanderer'.

title: Etched Glass Detail at Entry Gate
Front Door Detail
description: The new front door at this remodel re-uses the douglas fir joists from the original house, and was designed to admit light while giving privacy with glass blocks etched with a design, and inset into the wood frame.  This detail repeats the similar detail at the entry gate to the house and garden.

title: Palm as sculpture
description: This Windmill Palm is intended to both screen views from the neighbors house into the garden, making the jacuzzi more private, as well as soften the view from the jacuzzi looking back up to the house which towers above.

title: View of Front Entry Pergoal and street plantings
description: The structure at the gate was designed to mirror the new raised entry hall and stairwell at the house, and also give a bit of visual interest to a very tight front entry garden.  The walls were critical to giving some privacy to the newly created below ground floor bedrooms and bath fronting the street.  The walls step with the slope to not appear too massive, and a narrow planting strip between the wall and sidewalk allows just enough room for a few vines and shubs.

title: Clerodendron trichotomum variegata and Mathiasella blupueroides
Brahea 'Clara'
description: This Brahea is surely one of the most elegant ones for beautiful foliage, having the same powdery white silver foliage of a Brahea armata, while also having larger more elegant weeping foliage.  A bonus is the much faster growth under cooler summer conditions, which is invaluable for the local Bay Area conditions.  If I have more sun in my own garden, I would surely have several of these in my own garden.  Alas, it just isn't as suitable for shaded locations, really wanting the sun.

title: Bathroom with a private view
description: This is the view from inside the house at the newly created below grade addition added in this house remodel.  The view from the bathroom is out to the front yard enclosed courtyard to the north, and also has a captured view of the entry walk to the right.  The design was intended to give privacy and light to the below grade rooms, while also giving views out into the garden.  Without the privacy wall at the street, passersby would have direct views down into this window.  More typical foundation plantings would also have made the room darker with no real views.

title: Contrasts
description: The bare stripped trunk of the Windmill Palm has beautiful character and color if one takes the time to remove the fiber. The single touch of orange color is perfect against the pale green trunk.

title: Hanging gardens in Berkeley
description: Design by David Feix.  The large cantilevered deck off the upper level of the kitchen was designed to capture the views, both of the oak woodlands of the surroundings, the distant views of the Bay Bridge and downtown San Francisco, and to give views down into the garden below.  The design incorporated built-in planters alternating with wrought iron railing to make it seem a bit  more secure from this height, while also allowing more views straight out from the house.  The wood added to the underside of the deck was an aesthetic choice to give some contrast to the white walls.

title: Grand stairway from jacuzzi to mid level terrace
description: Somehow the addition of this one curving element within a house and garden entirely designed around various repeating patterns of squares and rectangles is visually and intellectually satisfying to me.  I think the twisting contorted arms of the Euphorbia ammak variegata at the terrace are a nice visual terminus to this view, and the Euphorbia will only get more dramatic in time as it gets ever larger against that blank wall.

title: Looking down from mid level terrace
Room with a view
description: I like how this terrace reads as an extension of the indoor room, and gets you out into the garden at tree top level, and looks into forest rather than the other homes that are just 75 feet away in this shot.

title: View of kitchen counter at breakfast nook
Nidularium innocentii and Chamaedorea tepejilote palm
description: This raised planter is immediately on the inside of the front gate, and marks the transition and grade change stepping down to the front  courtyard to the left.

title: Living room looking towards entry tower
Vriesea 'Hawaiian Sunset Hybrids'
description: These bromeliads simply light up when they catch the sun.

title: View across lower garden to far seat wall and patio
description: The foreground is planted with Arctotis 'Purple Torch' and Sedum palmeri, with a flowering Dyckia 'Cactus Ranch Red' beyond.

title: Trachycarpus fortunei leaves
description: View from inside the jacuzzi looking back up to the kitchen.

title: View across lower garden from jacuzzi
Shade plantings for color and texture
description: The plants used here have year round good looks and foliage color, even though only one, the Abutilon, is in bloom.  the Vriesea bromeliads will eventually get about 3 feet across, and the yellow foliaged Iresine herbstii is a great shade plant to lighten up a dark corner.  The overhanging foliage belongs to the Clerodendrum trichotomum 'Harlequin' in the adjacent planter to the left.
